name: Process Piping — Fabrication to Reinstatement

activities: underground trenches and thrust blocks for buried lines
sequence.note: Civil enters only as the enabler that supports the pipe.

activities: shop spool fabrication: cut, bevel, fit-up, shop weld
sequence.note: Most weld volume is prefabricated; see pipe_spool_fabrication.

activities: install permanent shoes, guides, anchors, rigid/spring hangers on steel and foundations
sequence.note: Supports must exist before the spool can land.

activities: rig and set spools onto supports
PWHT of field welds where required
chemical cleaning / pickling / passivation per service
sequence.note: Removes fabrication and test debris that would damage equipment and valves.

activities: install in-line items: control valves, orifice plates, PSVs, strainers, instruments
commission the line with its system
sequence.note: Exact order of alignment/piping/E&I steps varies by equipment and service.

typical_relationships.reason: the spool has nowhere to land until its permanent supports and hangers exist
erection of a specific spool cannot precede its fabrication and QC release
a weld must physically exist before it can be radiographed or ultrasonically tested
a rejected or un-heat-treated weld fails the pressure test; testing an unaccepted joint wastes the test

typical_relationships.after: fabricate/erect final tie-in spool to its nozzle
typical_relationships.reason: the closure spool is fitted to the as-set nozzle position, not the drawing position

typical_relationships.after: reinstate in-line items (control valves, orifices, PSVs, instruments)
typical_relationships.reason: these items are removed or spooled-out for the pressure test and cleaning to protect them from debris and over-pressure

typical_relationships.after: commission the line with process fluid
typical_relationships.reason: residual debris damages rotating equipment, control valves and instruments once fluid flows
pre-commissioning cannot start on a line that is not complete, clean, tested and reinstated
test water is generally introduced and removed before final cleaning/reinstatement, though some services flush first — order varies by spec
material identity and hardness are confirmed before pressurising alloy/CRA systems
insulation over joints that will still be broken for reinstatement has to be removed and redone

interfaces.requirement: support/rack steel erected, surveyed and bolted-up before piping is supported on it
equipment and support foundations, embeds, anchor bolts and buried-line trenches/thrust blocks ready before support install and buried-line laying
equipment set, aligned and grouted before final tie-in spools; nozzle-load / spring-hanger checks before coupling to sensitive equipment
pump/compressor/turbine set and aligned; piping strain-free with nozzle-load check before final bolt-up to protect alignment
in-line instruments (orifices, control valves, thermowells, PSVs) reinstated after cleaning and before the line is live
painting after weld NDT; insulation after hydrotest and reinstatement
test-water supply and disposal, N2 for purging/inerting, plant air for blowing available for testing and pre-commissioning
electric heat tracing installed after piping and before insulation

testing_requirements: Shop and field weld NDT per spec (VT + RT/UT/PT/MT) accepted to code (e.g. ASME B31.3)
PWHT and post-heat-treatment hardness survey where material/thickness requires
PMI (positive material identification) for alloy and CRA materials
Hydrostatic test per test package (typically 1.5x design), with hold time and pressure chart; pneumatic only where permitted
Flushing / air blowing / chemical cleaning / pickling-passivation per service class
Flange management: joint register with bolt torque/tension records
Reinstatement verification: in-line items fitted, orifice orientation, PSV set-pressure certificates
commissioning_dependencies: Subsystem mechanical completion / line-walk punch cleared
All in-line items reinstated with spades/spectacle blinds in the correct position
Flushing and cleaning certificate closed — system clean and dry
Connected equipment mechanically complete and commissioning-ready
Utilities available (N2, instrument air, flushing/cooling medium)
Relief protection in place and PSVs certified before pressurising with process fluid
Associated control/ESD loops live for the system
typical_exceptions: Large-bore buried process lines hydrotested before backfill so civil sequencing overrides
Pneumatic testing substituted where water is prohibited (dry service, tall columns, offshore weight limits)
Stainless/alloy lines skip PWHT but add pickling/passivation
Golden/tie-in joints left open until adjacent systems ready and tested by alternative means

work_packages.note: welding and inspection are separate responsibilities on the same joint

evidence: A process line was hydrotested and cleaned before its in-line control valves, orifices and relief valves were reinstated, and before the connected equipment reached mechanical completion — pre-commissioning cannot start on a line that is not complete, clean, tested and reinstated.
